outcome: No progress found: whether there are infinitely many cluster primes remains open, with no new results, bound improvements, or AI involvement located since 26 January 2024.
summary: Cluster primes (Blecksmith, Erdős, Selfridge 1999) are primes p such that every even integer up to p−3 is a difference of two primes ≤ p; whether infinitely many exist is listed as Erdős Problem #17. Checking erdosproblems.com/17 (last edited 28 December 2025) confirms the problem is explicitly marked open and notes it 'cannot be resolved with a finite computation' — no proof, partial resolution, or new bound has been posted. Its single forum comment (from Ribenboim, historical, predating the window) adds no new information. The Wikipedia 'Cluster prime' article still states plainly that it is not known whether there are infinitely many cluster primes, with its most recent cited research from 1999 (Blecksmith reciprocal-sum finiteness) and 2003 (Elsholtz's improved density bound), both well before the window. I searched specifically for any post-2024 tightening of the Blecksmith–Erdős–Selfridge/Elsholtz density bounds (which would count as `progress` per §3.1, since the record for 'how sparse are cluster primes' is closer to the actual open question than a mere existence search) and found nothing: no arXiv preprint, paper, or announcement referencing 'cluster primes' appears from 2024 onward in any of several searches. Searches for AI involvement (theorem provers, LLM-assisted proofs, GPT/Claude-related number theory results) turned up only unrelated material (a Riecoin 'cluster' cryptocurrency-mining hit, general AI-theorem-proving surveys like APOLLO/SorryDB/Gauss's Lean formalization of the prime number theorem) with no mention of cluster primes specifically. This is a clean 'nothing happened' case: the denominator problem is real and well-defined, but no mathematical or AI-related event touched it in the window.
competing_reading: None found. There is no plausible alternative classification; the only judgment call was whether to search for bound improvements (as a `progress`-eligible event distinct from the existence question itself) rather than stopping at the existence question, which I did and which also came up empty.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or paper improving the Elsholtz-era density/upper-bound estimates on cluster primes, or any argument bearing on the infinitude question, posted to arXiv or elsewhere after 26 January 2024; alternatively, an update to erdosproblems.com/17 or the Wikipedia article reflecting new work.
